1.explanation:
• FilterableMultiSelect.js reads the `id` prop and derives multiple element IDs (label, input, menu), so duplicate props produce duplicate DOM IDs. It also uses `<div role='group'>` for the menu container.  
• MultiSelect.js shares much of the ID-generation logic and should be aligned.  
• MultiSelect-story.js defines two FilterableMultiSelect examples with the same id, so needs updating to use unique ids or auto-id generation.  
• ListBoxField.js and ListBoxMenu.js/ ListBoxMenuItem.js set ARIA roles on the wrapper, menu, and menu items: options end up outside a true role="listbox" container. These components must ensure the proper wrapper role (listbox) for options.  
• internal/useId.js provides unique id generation and should be integrated so that when an id prop is reused, the component auto-generates unique IDs to avoid collisions.
1.bug_scenario: In the Filterable variant of the MultiSelect component (as shown in the Carbon React storybook), rendering two instances with the same `id` prop causes duplicate HTML `id` attributes on the wrapper, label, input, and menu elements. This triggers DAP violations (“Element 'id' attribute values must be unique”) and ARIA errors (“role='option' must be contained within an element with role='listbox'”). The FilterableMultiSelect uses its `id` prop to build multiple sub-IDs and renders its options inside a `<div role="group">` rather than a `listbox`, so options with role="option" are in an invalid parent.

2.explanation: FilterableMultiSelect.js is responsible for rendering the filterable dropdown, including assigning the base id to the label, input, and menu. It currently passes the same user-provided id to both instances, producing duplicate IDs. MultiSelect.js contains shared logic for id‐based ARIA attributes (listbox, option roles) that are mis-scoped when the id is duplicated. MultiSelectPropTypes.js defines the id prop requirement and could enforce uniqueness or warn. internal/useId.js provides the default unique id generation logic when no id is passed; updating these files to merge user id with a unique suffix (or warn on duplicates) will fix the accessibility errors.
2.bug_scenario: When rendering two MultiSelect.Filterable components with the same “id” prop (in this case “carbon-multiselect-example”), the HTML DOM ends up with duplicate id attributes and ARIA roles applied to elements outside of a valid listbox container. The DAP scan reports “Element ‘id’ attribute values must be unique within a document” and multiple “option” roles not contained within a role=“listbox” parent. The screenshot shows two <input> elements and multiple menu items all sharing the same id values, leading to accessibility violations.
